root: ^A king found himself in a desperate bid to save his kingdom.
^ In his desperation, he enlisted the help of a mage from a faraway land.
^ A scholar in elemental magic, this mage raised an army of indestructible stone knights to protect the kingdom against all threats.
^Many battles ensued, and in all of them, the stone warriors brought victory back home.
^As their power grew, however, the king's land began to wither, with famine spreading like a disease.
^The mage had been drawing power from the soil and water to source his knights' mana costs.
^The king, after this revelation, ordered the mage to destroy his stone army.
^Alas, it was too late, for the stone army had grown far too powerful for the mage's hand.
^The king then devised a secret plan with the other wizards of his court.
^The mage was ordered to travel with his stone army to a nearby cavern inhabited by bandits.
^As they worked to clear the evil pillagers from the cavern,
^ the place was sealed and buried with magic by the king's wizards.
^And so, the mage was imprisoned with his stone army,
^ destined to slumber eternally beneath the bedrock of Snailcliff Mountain.
^In the tongue of elves, it means "one who shapes stones."
^Some say he met an accursed death and theorize that he will return as a vengeful spirit, lying in wait for an innocent footstep mistakenly taken towards that cavern.
^Those who pass through Snailcliff swear they hear stone steps echoing in the mountain's rocks.
^What was once history has now become legend, and for some, it has transformed into a favorite tourist destination, the haunted road of Snailcliff.
